title.narrative: The Green Evolution: Pathways for food system Transformation

description.narrative: 5,000 smallholder farmer households with one farmer from each household (40% women) which will be clustered into 160 groups. 3,000 additional farmers reached out through climate information service;600 extension workers from relevant departments of state and national governmen.1,200 community members reached through food system dialogues and food system analysis (50% women); 10 food business operators (micro level.25 elected representatives (members of parliament, members of the legislative authority) and 100 officials from the agriculture/horticulture/livestock/fisheries/rural development/food sectors at the district, state and national levels;600 advisors from the fields of agriculture/horticulture/livestock/fisheries/rural development/nutrition at the level of districts. or lower administrative units under federal/national governments.200 students (50% women) and 35 members of civil society (40% women), who will take on the role of multipliers, will be reached through capacity building.Altogether, the program will reach out to approximately 10,295 and in total, the programme is expected to reach 249,900 people indirectly.

Overall objective (Impact) Support the implementation of national strategies in Nepal for equitable, resilient and sustainable food systems.Programme Objective: Local agroecological food systems in Nepal will be strengthened through improved policy frameworks, operational structures and multi-stakeholder cooperation at all levels.

This is a multi-country project to be implemented in India (lead), Nepal and Bangladesh. In Nepal, the project will directly work with 5000 farming households in addtion to government agri-extension workers and agroecology value chain intermediaries. The project will be implemented in Jumla, Dailekh and Surkhet districts of Karnali province. The overall aim of the project is to promote agro-eocology to strengthen local food systems and will address the issues at micro, meso and macro levels.
